route.change: Think-SFT (no reward) with the cue, token cap raised to 32,768, three samples per problem scored by a sequential vote (take samples 1 and 2 if their answers agree, else add sample 3; plurality, ties to the shortest finished sample).
route.gap_parts: Capability: the base never solves about 79 hard328 problems even after restarts, and Think-SFT's wider reach covers part of that (one sample 212 against the base's 161). Budget (cap hit; 0.21 to 0.27 of the gross gap in result-f39ba8): on hard328, raising Think-SFT's cap from 16,384 to 32,768 adds about 23 (207 to 230), and on MATH-500 about 1 to 3. Reliability (0.43 to 0.67 of the gap): the vote adds about 15 to 20 on hard328 (vote over 4 at cap 16k gave 212 to 241) and about 15 on MATH-500 (461 to 481). Full-set forecast about 247 of 328 at about 35,400 generated tokens, against 241 for the best known row at 30,904 to 40,410 tokens.
route.why: Weight edits and votes only reweight paths the host already has, so their gains stop near the host's pass@k; a host with more reach (Think-SFT) raises that ceiling. A longer cap lets its long contest derivations finish, and the vote then turns its reach into right answers.
